title: tldraw.computer - Steve Ruiz, tldraw
talk_summary: Steve Ruiz demos tldraw's AI experiments: screenshot-to-app generation (Make Real), a node-graph 'computer' where each block is a small LLM prompt with typed inputs/outputs, and canvas manipulation via structured text output rather than pixels. The talk is mostly product demo with little engineering detail on reliability, cost, or orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Typed-input/output prompt blocks in a graph
takeaways.what_they_do: Each node has a tiny fixed instruction ('Analyze inputs... based on the inputs, write the text... output the result') and emits data in a shape the next node accepts, so nodes compose without shared context.
When a generated app showed a visual bug, they captured a screenshot of the defect and sent it alongside the original source with a targeted 'fix that particular bug' prompt.

takeaways.technique: Structured text output mapped to app state
takeaways.what_they_do: The model returns a text structure that the app maps into canvas shapes, so the model's output is editable and correctable by the human rather than a raster image.

takeaways.technique: Cheap fast multimodal model for high-volume nodes
takeaways.what_they_do: They built the graph on Gemini Flash specifically because it was fast and 'pretty good' and multimodal, rather than the largest model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Gemini Flash was out and Flash was fast and pretty good and multimodal. So, that was the kind of the inspiration
